prerequisites: Must have passed the Drawing course.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand and possess knowledge.
Application of knowledge.
Ability to make judgments.
Basic knowledge of the profession.
Ability to solve problems.
Ethical commitment.
Ability to manage specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Ability to analyze and evaluate the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Ability to apply quality principles and methods.
Ability to organize and plan in the field of business, and other institutions and organizations.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Basic knowledge and application of environmental technologies and sustainability.
Applied knowledge of business organization.
Knowledge and abilities to organize and manage projects.
Knowledge of the organizational structure and functions of a technical office.
Acquire the basic-fundamental knowledge of the project process, elaboration, and management of projects and works within their professional competencies.
Students are expected to have sufficient knowledge, at a theoretical and practical level, to face both the drafting, programming, and management of engineering projects.
Inform the student about the responsibilities derived from the drafting and execution of projects and the role of the engineer in the current social context.
Be able to correctly draft a classic project.

Know and be able to intervene in or draft other documents that may be part of the project or are a consequence of it, such as a Safety and Health study, environmental impact studies, or industrial activity projects.
Be instructed in the main administrative procedures derived from project management.

teaching_methods: Conduct virtual individual and collective tutorials
assessment_rules: For ordinary call (continuous assessment), continuous evaluation (two questionnaires) accounts for 60% (54% theoretical, 6% practical) and a final theoretical-practical exam accounts for 40%. Both continuous assessment (50% of maximum points) and the final exam (50% of maximum points) must be passed independently. Class attendance affects the final grade with a factor between 0 and 1. Students can opt for a single final exam (non-continuous assessment) comprising a theory part (60% of the final grade, must get 50% of maximum points) and a practical part (40% of the final grade, must get 50% of maximum points). The extraordinary call evaluation will be similar to the non-continuous ordinary call, covering all content blocks and competencies.
